question:
DRAG DROP -
Drag and drop the HyperFlex characteristics from the left onto the appropriate HyperFlex node types on the right.
bank: uses only SSD drives for caching
contains HDDs for the capacity layer
uses SSD drives or NVMe storage for caching
recommended for repeatable and sustainable high performance, especially for scenarios with a larger working set of data
has SSD drives for the capacity layer
recommended for capacity sensitive solutions, lower budgets, and fewer performance-sensitive applications
theory: HyperFlex Hybrid nodes use SSDs purely for the caching layer and HDDs for the capacity layer, which is why Cisco recommends them for capacity-sensitive solutions, lower-budget deployments, and workloads that are not especially performance-sensitive. All-Flash (and NVMe-capable) nodes instead use SSD or NVMe storage for both caching and the capacity tier, giving them the low, consistent latency needed for repeatable, sustainable high performance — especially valuable when the active working set of data is larger than what a caching tier alone could absorb. (Note: per Cisco's official HyperFlex documentation, the phrase 'capacity sensitive, lower budgets, fewer performance-sensitive applications' describes Hybrid nodes, and 'repeatable and sustainable high performance ... larger working set of data' describes All-Flash nodes — this differs from the pairing currently stored for two of the six items in this question's answer key.) (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 15 — HyperFlex Hybrid vs. All-Flash Nodes)
